chunks: Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who dies while only women are present with him. He said: “A woman who is his mahram should perform ghusl for him, and the women should pour water for her, and she should not remove his garment. And if it is a woman who dies among men, and there is no woman with her and no mahram for her, then she should be buried as she is in her clothes. And if a mahram of hers is with her, he should perform ghusl for her over her clothes.”

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهُ: she performs the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment, which is not to be removed during the washing
key_terms.ثِيَابِهَا: her clothes, in which she remains if no qualified washer is present
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman who is within the prohibited degree of marriage to him, permitting this handling
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male mahram relative permitted to handle her body in this restricted context
key_terms.مِنْ فَوْقِ ثِيَابِهَا: over her clothes, without uncovering her body

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing ghusl for a deceased man or woman when only the opposite sex is present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings for handling the deceased when only members of the opposite sex are present. It specifies the role of a mahram in ghusl and preserves bodily covering through clothing in such circumstances.
